text:
Maria: Hey team — customer 'AcmeMed' on Private is hitting repeated failures when we try to upload debug bundles from the collector. Collector logs show 'redaction mismatch: sensitive fields remaining' then process exits. presign endpoint returns 403 for the final PUT. Need quick repro steps and what to collect.

Aj: Thanks — can you drop the collector version + the redact config they used? Also the request id from the presign call if available.

Maria: collector v2.8.1, redact config: /etc/redwood/redact.yaml (policy: pii-basic). Request id from presign service: r-sd9f8a2. Customer tried both browser upload and the in-collector upload.

Nate: Two parallel things to check: 1) whether redaction tool actually ran (collector should produce a .redacted manifest) and 2) whether the presign response included x-amz-region header mismatch (we've seen 403 when region mismatched). Can you paste the exact curl they used?

Maria: They ran the helper in the UI which calls presign then PUT. Here's the curl we captured from the customer packet capture:

```
curl -X PUT "https://s3.signed-example.com/upload/abcd" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \n  --upload-file /tmp/debugbundle.tar.gz -v
```

Cole: If the collector failed redaction it may have left a partially redacted file. Ask them for the collector stdout/stderr and the collector.manifest in the bundle. Also check collector started with the same redact config path — sometimes override via env REDACT_CONFIG.

Maria: Pasted collector stderr snippet: 

```
2026-05-12T14:22:11Z ERROR redactor: remaining fields: [ssn, card_number]
2026-05-12T14:22:11Z INFO uploader: presign request id=r-sd9f8a2
2026-05-12T14:22:12Z WARN uploader: presign returned 403 (SignatureDoesNotMatch)
2026-05-12T14:22:12Z ERROR collector: upload failed, exiting
```

Aj: SignatureDoesNotMatch often indicates either clock skew or wrong signing key/region. Steps for repro: 1) run collector locally with `--dry-run --output /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz` to get the bundle without upload, 2) run the redactor locally: `redact-tool --input /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz --config /etc/redwood/redact.yaml --verify` — the `--verify` prints remaining fields. Share output.

Nate: Also try reproducing upload using the presign response directly. After collector dry-run, do: 

```
# request presign (use the same presign API the collector calls)
curl -X POST "https://private-console.example.com/api/v1/presign" -d '{"name":"db","size":12345}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
# take returned url and headers
curl -X PUT '<returned_url>' -H 'x-amz-date: 20260512T142213Z' -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --upload-file /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz -v
```

Cole: If that PUT returns 403, capture full response headers. Check Date header on the presign and client machine time (`date -u`). If clock differs by >5m AWS sigv4 fails. If time looks fine, capture the presign payload and check x-amz-credential (region) vs S3 endpoint.

Maria: Customer says their VM clock is synced to corporate NTP. They do have an HSM/KMS rotation last week — could that matter?

Aj: KMS rotation affects server-side encryption keys but not presign sig itself. However, if the presign service was signed with an old credential that's rotated out, you'd see SignatureDoesNotMatch and request ids. Ask security to confirm service principal/key hasn't been rotated in presign service.

support-bot: Reminder: attach collector binary, collector.manifest, redact.yaml, and full stderr/stdout logs. Use secure upload link or SFTP fallback. See runbook /runbooks/private-debug-bundle.md

Maria: Customer tried SFTP fallback but their SFTP server rejects the incoming connection over port 22 from our worker pool. They can open outbound SSH though. Suggestion?

Nate: If direct SFTP inbound is blocked, we can instruct them to scp the bundle to our bastion. Steps: on their VM:

```
# create dry-run bundle
/opt/redwood/bin/collector --collect --dry-run --output /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz --include-logs --include-manifest
# scp to redwood bastion
scp /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz redwood@bastion.private.redwood.com:/uploads/acmemed/
```

If scp isn't possible, they can gzip and split and upload via HTTPS chunked curl to a temporary customer support bucket we create.

Cole: Also run `collector inspect-manifest --verify /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz` — this will fail early with a list of unredacted fields and line numbers. If unredacted fields persist, ask them to run with `--redact-level strict` and re-run.

Maria: I'll ask them to produce the dry-run bundle, run redact-tool --verify, grab presign output, and if upload fails do scp to bastion. I'll paste results here.

(15m later) Maria: Uploaded the dry-run bundle to our bastion via scp. Collector.inspect-manifest shows two remaining fields (card_number, ssn) with paths in logs. They ran `redact-tool --input /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz --config /etc/redwood/redact.yaml --fix` and then `--verify` shows clean. Re-ran upload using the original presign url and now PUT succeeded.

Aj: Nice — so root cause was collector redactor not being applied in their initial run (env override). Please record steps we used in the ticket: dry-run -> redact-tool --fix -> presign reuse -> PUT success. Close after they confirm ingestion.

Maria: Customer confirmed ingestion and gave us the original presign request id (r-sd9f8a2). Marking resolved. :party_parrot:
